group.passage:
Scientists who study the ocean’s fish do not try to count every fish in the sea. Instead, they divide fish into stocks: populations of one species that share an area and grow and die at similar rates. A stock works a little like money in a savings account. Fishers can keep taking from it year after year without using it up, as long as they take no more than the fish can replace by breeding and growing. When the catch goes beyond that limit, known as the maximum sustainable yield, the population is counted as overfished.
By this measure, the world’s oceans have been slowly losing ground. The chart below, based on figures from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations, shows how the fish populations that scientists have studied are divided between the two groups. In 1974, only one in ten was overfished; by 2021, the figure was more than one in three.
Yet these figures do not tell the whole story. In 2025, the FAO published its most detailed review so far, covering 2,570 stocks and drawing on more than 650 experts. It found that 64.5 percent of them were being fished within safe limits. When each population was weighted by the amount of fish it actually supplies, however, the share rose to 77.2 percent of all the fish landed. Tuna offer a clear example: 87 percent of tuna populations were in good shape, and they provided 99 percent of the tuna brought ashore.
Location matters as well. In the Northeast Pacific, where fishing has long been closely controlled, 92.7 percent of stocks were healthy, compared with only 35.1 percent in the Mediterranean and Black Sea. Even there, though, cutting fishing pressure by 30 percent since 2013 has allowed the total weight of fish to grow by 15 percent. One warning remains: all of these numbers describe only the stocks that have been checked, and many off the coasts of Africa, Asia, and South America have never been studied at all. The true picture may therefore be better or worse than the chart suggests.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: Why tuna are easier to protect than most other kinds of ocean fish.
options.B: How the Mediterranean and Black Sea recovered from years of overfishing.
options.C: How healthy the world’s fish stocks are, and why one figure can mislead.
options.D: Why scientists divide fish into stocks instead of trying to count every fish.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why the share rose to 77.2 percent when each population was weighted by the fish it supplies?

options.A: Many overfished populations have never been studied at all.
options.B: The 2025 review covered more stocks than any earlier study.
options.C: Fishers stopped landing fish from overfished populations after 2021.
options.D: Healthy populations tend to supply more fish than overfished ones.

questions.stem: According to the chart, which of the following is true?

options.A: By 2021, the overfished share was more than three times its 1974 level.
options.B: The overfished share went up between every two years shown on the chart.
options.C: The share within sustainable levels fell by over 20 points from 1974 to 2000.
options.D: The overfished share rose more from 2000 to 2008 than from 1990 to 2000.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention the 30 percent cut in fishing pressure in the Mediterranean and Black Sea?

options.A: To show that the region now has more healthy stocks than the Northeast Pacific.
options.B: To show that even a badly overfished region can improve when fishing is reduced.
options.C: To point out a weakness in the way the FAO collects and reports its data.
options.D: To explain why tuna populations are in better shape than other fish.

1.explanation_zh: 第一、二段說明什麼是過度捕撈，並指出過度捕撈的比例從 1974 年的十分之一升到 2021 年超過三分之一；第三段用 Yet these figures do not tell the whole story 轉折：依漁獲量加權後，永續的比例更高；第四段再說地點不同差異很大，而且數字只涵蓋評估過的魚群。全文在說「世界的魚群狀況如何，以及只看單一數字為什麼會失真」。
evidence: By this measure, the world’s oceans have been slowly losing ground.
Yet these figures do not tell the whole story.
The true picture may therefore be better or worse than the chart suggests.

option_notes_zh.A: 以偏概全：鮪魚只是第三段的一個例子，文中也沒有比較鮪魚和其他魚哪一種比較好保護。
option_notes_zh.B: 以偏概全，而且說過頭：地中海只在第四段出現，它的永續比例仍只有 35.1%，文中只說魚的總重量增加，沒有說已經恢復。
option_notes_zh.D: 以偏概全：只涵蓋第一段的定義；後面三段談的都是全球魚群的狀況與數字的解讀。

A: Tuna offer a clear example: 87 percent of tuna populations were in good shape, and they provided 99 percent of the tuna brought ashore.
B: In the Northeast Pacific, where fishing has long been closely controlled, 92.7 percent of stocks were healthy, compared with only 35.1 percent in the Mediterranean and Black Sea.
Even there, though, cutting fishing pressure by 30 percent since 2013 has allowed the total weight of fish to grow by 15 percent.
D: Instead, they divide fish into stocks: populations of one species that share an area and grow and die at similar rates.

1.strategy_zh: 主旨題要涵蓋大多數段落：先抓轉折句（Yet these figures do not tell the whole story），正解通常是較抽象的概括；只講一段的例子（鮪魚、地中海、定義）都要排除。
hints: 第二段說世界的魚群整體上變好還是變差？
第三段開頭的 Yet 之後，作者想提醒讀者什麼？
第四段最後一句說圖表呈現的情況一定準確嗎？

2.explanation_zh: 以魚群「數目」算，永續的只有 64.5%；改用每個魚群實際提供的漁獲量加權後，永續魚群提供了 77.2% 的漁獲。加權後比例變高，表示健康的魚群平均提供的漁獲比過度捕撈的多。鮪魚是例子：87% 的鮪魚魚群狀況良好，卻提供了 99% 的鮪魚漁獲。
evidence: It found that 64.5 percent of them were being fished within safe limits.
When each population was weighted by the amount of fish it actually supplies, however, the share rose to 77.2 percent of all the fish landed.
Tuna offer a clear example: 87 percent of tuna populations were in good shape, and they provided 99 percent of the tuna brought ashore.

option_notes_zh.A: 這是第四段對所有數字的提醒（只涵蓋評估過的魚群），和「加權後比例上升」無關；未評估的魚群根本不在 64.5% 或 77.2% 的計算裡。
option_notes_zh.B: 答非所問：報告涵蓋的魚群多寡（2,570 個）不能解釋同一份報告中兩個比例的差異。
option_notes_zh.C: 文中沒有說漁民在 2021 年後停止捕撈過度捕撈的魚群；加權的比例反而顯示仍有約兩成多的漁獲來自不永續的魚群。

A: One warning remains: all of these numbers describe only the stocks that have been checked, and many off the coasts of Africa, Asia, and South America have never been studied at all.
B: In 2025, the FAO published its most detailed review so far, covering 2,570 stocks and drawing on more than 650 experts.

2.strategy_zh: 推論題先寫出兩個數字各自算的是什麼（魚群數目 vs. 漁獲量），再想「怎樣的情況會讓第二個比第一個大」；用文中的例子（鮪魚）驗證。
hints: 64.5% 是以什麼為單位算的？77.2% 又是以什麼為單位？
如果健康魚群和過度捕撈魚群提供的漁獲一樣多，兩個比例會怎樣？
鮪魚的例子：87% 的魚群提供了多少比例的漁獲？

3.explanation_zh: 過度捕撈的比例在 1974 年是 10%，2021 年是 35.5%，是 1974 年的 3.55 倍，所以超過三倍。其他選項：2008 年 33% 到 2013 年 32% 是下降，不是每一段都上升；永續比例從 1974 年的 90% 降到 2000 年的 72.8%，只少了 17.2 個百分點；2000 到 2008 年增加 5.8 個百分點，比 1990 到 2000 年的 9.1 個百分點少。
evidence: 1974, Overfished: 10%
2021, Overfished: 35.5%

option_notes_zh.B: 只看整體趨勢：2008 年 33% 到 2013 年 32%，這一段是下降的。
option_notes_zh.C: 計算錯誤：90 − 72.8 ＝ 17.2，沒有超過 20 個百分點。

3.strategy_zh: 圖表題要動手算：「幾倍」用除法（35.5 ÷ 10），「降了幾個百分點」用減法，「每一段都上升」要逐段檢查，「哪一段增加較多」要兩段都算出來比較。
hints: 1974 年和 2021 年 Overfished 各是多少？35.5 是 10 的幾倍？
2008 年到 2013 年，Overfished 是上升還是下降？

4.explanation_zh: 第四段先說地中海與黑海只有 35.1% 的魚群健康，是表現很差的區域；接著用 Even there 說，自 2013 年以來捕撈壓力降低 30%，魚的總重量就增加了 15%。作者舉這個例子，是要說明即使是過度捕撈嚴重的海域，減少捕撈也能改善。
evidence: In the Northeast Pacific, where fishing has long been closely controlled, 92.7 percent of stocks were healthy, compared with only 35.1 percent in the Mediterranean and Black Sea.
Even there, though, cutting fishing pressure by 30 percent since 2013 has allowed the total weight of fish to grow by 15 percent.

option_notes_zh.A: 與原文相反：地中海與黑海的健康比例（35.1%）遠低於東北太平洋（92.7%）。
option_notes_zh.C: 答非所問：資料的限制是下一句才提到的另一件事（只涵蓋評估過的魚群），和捕撈壓力降低的例子無關。
option_notes_zh.D: 細節錯置：鮪魚是第三段的例子，和地中海減少捕撈無關。

A: In the Northeast Pacific, where fishing has long been closely controlled, 92.7 percent of stocks were healthy, compared with only 35.1 percent in the Mediterranean and Black Sea.
C: One warning remains: all of these numbers describe only the stocks that have been checked, and many off the coasts of Africa, Asia, and South America have never been studied at all.
D: Tuna offer a clear example: 87 percent of tuna populations were in good shape, and they provided 99 percent of the tuna brought ashore.

4.strategy_zh: 目的題看連接詞：Even there（即使在那裡）表示「讓步＋出乎意料的好消息」，作者用它說明改善是可能的；緊接在後的另一句（One warning remains）是另一個重點，不要混在一起。
hints: 地中海與黑海的魚群健康比例和東北太平洋比起來如何？
Even there 後面說發生了什麼變化？
減少捕撈壓力和魚的總重量增加之間是什麼關係？

translation_zh.text:
研究海洋魚類的科學家並不會去數海裡的每一條魚。他們把魚分成「魚群」（stock）：同一個物種、生活在同一海域、生長與死亡速度相近的族群。魚群有點像存款帳戶。只要每年捕撈的量不超過魚靠繁殖和成長所能補回的量，漁民就能年復一年地捕撈而不把它用光。捕撈量一旦超過這個上限——也就是所謂的「最大永續產量」——這個族群就被算作過度捕撈。
依這個標準，世界的海洋一直在慢慢失守。下圖根據聯合國糧食及農業組織（FAO）的數字，顯示科學家研究過的魚群在兩類之間的分布。1974 年，十個魚群中只有一個過度捕撈；到了 2021 年，比例已超過三分之一。
然而，這些數字並沒有說出全貌。2025 年，FAO 發表了迄今最詳盡的評估，涵蓋 2,570 個魚群，有超過 650 位專家參與。評估發現，64.5% 的魚群是在安全範圍內捕撈。不過，若依每個族群實際提供的漁獲量加權，這個比例會升到全部上岸漁獲的 77.2%。鮪魚就是明顯的例子：87% 的鮪魚族群狀況良好，而它們提供了 99% 的上岸鮪魚。
地點也有影響。在長期嚴格管理捕撈的東北太平洋，92.7% 的魚群是健康的；相較之下，地中海與黑海只有 35.1%。但即使在那裡，自 2013 年以來把捕撈壓力降低 30%，也讓魚的總重量增加了 15%。還有一點要提醒：這些數字都只描述經過評估的魚群，而非洲、亞洲和南美洲沿海還有許多魚群從未被研究過。因此，真實的情況可能比圖表顯示的更好，也可能更糟。
【圖】全球已評估魚群的狀況（1974–2021，%）：在永續範圍內／過度捕撈。

open_tasks.prompt: The passage says that places where fishing is closely controlled have healthier fish stocks. Suggest one rule Taiwan could use to protect a type of fish, and explain in 1–2 English sentences why it would help.
reference_answers: Taiwan could set a yearly limit on how much of one fish may be caught, because taking no more than the fish can replace keeps the stock from becoming overfished.
Taiwan could close some fishing areas during the months when the fish breed, so that more young fish survive and the population can grow again, as happened in the Mediterranean.
